concept.name: Weighted moving average
concept.definition: A moving average that weights observations linearly by recency — the newest price gets weight n, the next n-1, down to 1 — so recent data dominates while the window length stays fixed.
concept.intuition: A compromise between the SMA and EMA: recent prices matter more, but the weights decline in a straight line rather than exponentially.
concept.mechanics: Multiply each of the last n prices by its recency rank, sum the products, and divide by the sum of the weights n(n+1)/2. Recomputed fresh each bar; not recursive.
concept.formula: WMA(n) = sum(i * P_i, i=1..n) / sum(i, i=1..n), with P_n the most recent price; the denominator equals n(n+1)/2.
concept.failure_modes: Lags like all averages and whipsaws in ranges; the abrupt weight cutoff at the window edge makes it twitchy when a large old value exits the window.
concept.misconceptions: A WMA is not an EMA: WMA weights decline linearly over a fixed window, whereas EMA weights decay exponentially over an effectively infinite history.
concept.example: With closes 10, 11, 12, the 3-period WMA = (1*10 + 2*11 + 3*12)/6 = 68/6 = 11.33, versus an SMA of 11.

citations.source: What Is The Weighted Moving Average? - Fidelity Investments
